findings: The official Onset page-1 photograph shows a cream ribbed cylindrical adapter with hexagonal ends. The candidate now follows that form rather than borrowing the black S-THB adapter; dimensions remain inferred.

Official single-rotor and overall photos show short cup ribs. The primary 60 mm radius hypothesis follows those proportions more closely than the literal 108 mm model; the amber overlay keeps the unresolved source interpretation visible. This is not calibrated photogrammetry or manufacturer confirmation of an error.

Inspected side and head views retain the bent hollow arm, hourglass head, open cups, swept vane, separate brass nose, source-shaped saddle, real slots and hollow tube sleeve. Local profiles remain authored.
The base section shows actual bore and cable-groove cuts. A previous cable/rib penetration was removed with a real bottom exit and 10 mm turn; solid intersection checks reran.

The separate loose kit contains two pointed lag-screw envelopes and a continuous bent hexagonal key. Detached key/socket views correspond to isolated insertion checks, without assembled tool access or torque credit.
geometry_limits: Published cup radius, overall-size datums, 3 m / 12.2 m cable length and related Davis mass values remain conflicting.
Primary radius, adapter dimensions, bearings, cable rest poses, tool legs and local hardware dimensions are explicit hypotheses.
Cable meshes have continuous parallel-transport sections and measured polyline lengths, but no flexibility, gravity settling or retention qualification.
Tripod, guy wires, ground connection, installed cable routes and U30 mating remain incomplete. These are isolated candidate components, not laboratory initial stock.
